newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn using "tricks" to meet EMU target - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bonn using "tricks" to meet EMU target - paper.

text.p: The German government faces an explosion in the costs of pension payments for civil servants working in the former Deutsche Bundespost that could create an unexpected deficit of 7.4 billion marks by 1999, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The daily Frankfurter Rundschau (FR) said Bonn, concerned that plugging the unexpected gap in pension payments could ruin its bid to qualify for European economic and monetary union (EMU), resorted to "financing tricks" to resolve the problem.

The deficit pension payments are for civil servants now employed by Deutsche Telekom AG, Deutsche Post AG and Deutsche Postbank AG, that were spun off from the Bundespost in 1995 and slated for full privatisation in the next century.
Bonn agreed to take over the lion's share of pension payments for civil servants still working at the companies from the year 2000 and to finance any deficit in the pension fund.
But according to documents obtained by the paper, Bonn has worked out alternative financing that would hide the costs.
The paper said rather than fund the pension deficit directly, the pension fund would compensate the deficit initially by borrowing money from the companies that Bonn would have to pay back later.
The paper said the deficit for the Bundespost pension fund was expected to reach nearly 75 billion marks by 2010.
The post and telecommunications ministry said it would comment on the report later in the day.

Deutsche Telekom, which listed more than 25 percent of its capital on international stock exchanges last year, declined to comment on the report. A spokesman emphasised, however, that the government was liable for any pension fund deficits.
